title: Linux product stdlib loads a qualified OS ICU at runtime instead of linking ICU 76
goal: Fix intellibitz/susi#1667. The Linux product standard library linked libicuuc.so.76 and its _76 symbols, so the ship gate could not build on stock Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (ICU 74) and gate-built executables did not start without ICU 76. Load the newest qualified OS ICU (76 with Unicode 16.0, then 74 with Unicode 15.1) from the standard absolute system library directories at first use, hold the selected library to its exact recorded Unicode version, fail with a message naming both libraries when neither is present, and keep the Windows ICU 15.1 contract unchanged. Drop the ICU 76 DT_NEEDED entries from the reviewed ELF import list, since shipped executables no longer link ICU.

criteria: the trusted sysroot gate builds the product stdlib on a host with ICU 74 only, ICU 76 only, or both
the consumer test passes with ICU 76 and with ICU 74 as the only visible library, and identifies the loaded library from /proc/self/maps
with neither library visible, the first Unicode operation panics naming libicuuc.so.76 and libicuuc.so.74
gate-built executables have no libicuuc or libicudata DT_NEEDED entry
Windows keeps the raw-dylib icu.dll import and the Unicode 15.1 pin
